To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the endothelial cells are able to react on the presence of a tumor by forming cytoplasmatic protrusions and by developing cell edemas, which are visible by scanning and transmission electron microscopy.

endothelial cells in carcinomas of the maxilla show cytoplasmatic projections into the vascular lument and that the endothelial cells are mixed with tumor cells and erythroocytes, so that the vascular lumen can hardly be identified.
the endothelium of tumor vessels is characterized by a variety of ultrastructural changes and that the vascular lumen is frequently filled by tumor cells and/or erythrocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether or not a morphological reaction can be observed in the vascular system, and whether this is of any significance in the process of metastasis.
the question of whether a vascular system is still functional in tumors of the head and of the neck.
the question, whether the morphological changes of the vascular endothelium in carcinomas of the auricle and of the maxilla are of diagnostic value for the prognosis of the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vascular reaction is not a specific phenomenon of the tumor tissue, but a general reaction of the endothelial cells in the area of a tumor.
the vascular reaction is a complex process, which is not yet completely understood.
the endothelial cells of the tumor vessels are in a state of "permanent emergency" and are therefore not able to fulfill their function as a blood/lymphatic filter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endothelial cells of the tumor vessels show a variety of reactions, which are similar to those in normal vessels.
the vascular reaction of tumors in the head and neck area is similar to those in other parts of the body.
the endothelial cells are able to react to a noxious event, i.e. to a growing tumor, by developing cytoplasmatic projections into the lumen of the blood vessel, so that a "tumor vessel" is formed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endothelial cells in the vascular reaction of carcinomas of the auricle and the maxilla show ultrastructural changes which are comparable to the findings in carcinomas of other localizations.
the endothelial cells of tumor vessels are able to react in a similar way as in the normal vessels.
the endothelial cells of the tumor vasculature are capable to respond to noxa, as is the case in the normal vascular system, but the morphological reaction is less distinct and less pronounced.
